title: Language is the root of all evil
content: Picture this: a wild tiger breaks into a city and hunts, as it does insinctively, to sustain its everyday life. One day it stumbles into a human "home" and eats a human baby. The parents go hysteric: sorrow, regret, hatred and all other emotions flood them. News reports about a tiger on the loose eating babies terrorise the whole community and suddenly everyone protests to bring justice and bring an end to the tiger terror. Meanwhile the tiger goes on to find another food, and maybe feed its babies, and if its babies die from other predators while the tiger parent protects them, the tiger moves on. This goes to show that nature itself is not good or bad. Life and death continues as an endless natural cycle. Nature does not attach meaning to the sustenance of a tiger or the death of a human being. Something outside of nature, miraculously born from a specific being - that being humans - warps the virgin and innocent autonomy of nature. Symbols, meanings, ideas - language as such. Killing a human baby makes one a monster yet killing a tiger makes one a hero. Whoever decided that? Language distorts our symbolic dimension, the way we see and beleive what the world is - not what it literally is. The idea that "Tigers are monsters that terrorise civilised community" is greater, larger, and supersedes a literal living tiger who killed a baby. That very symbol or idea will lead to longlasting violent outbursts towards tigers. Here we can see the monstrosity of language. The very pronoun "it" is a label conjured by humans to refer to animals, which fundamentally saps out the subjective dimension of "that" creature, reducing "it" to an object of lower status; and our cunning way of returning "it" into a dignified subject worthy of our company and love is giving "it" a proper name such as Rocket for a pet raccoon and referring them with human pronouns. Such symbolic violence is far greater than the violence that is obvious to us because the former is the cause of the latter. Heck, some people even use "She/Her" to refer to their beloved car (isn't she a beauty?). A "home" is something greater than a house - it is where your create memories with people you love while a house is just somewhere you stay to shield yourself from environmental hazards. Here's an interesting idea: some dudes wrote books about a supreme all-knowing creature, His chosen people, and His Son, who for some reason, can turn water into wine, who ironically is Himself all along. People waged war and maintained peace simultaneously because of those books. Millions suffered miserably and millions lived fulfilling lives because of a collection of words. Language in a literal sense is like the "voice" possessed by Paul Muad'Dib Atreides from Dune, the Lissan al' Gaib, the chosen one. Language distorts reality, it is a phantasmatic anomaly that somehow invade and proliferate our deepest fears and desires, our ideas of good and evil, and ultimately our choices. Language is the root of all evil. But can language also be the root of all that is good? For me, good is nothing without evil. Good cannot exist by itself, it needs its opposite evil to maintain its status. Evil on the other hand is fundamental. Language perverted nature and we had to stabilise the monstrosity of such an act by inventing Good. Also I was not talking about tigers and babies.

title: I GOT A PENTAKILL WITH AZIR
content: Azir, one of the hardest champions in league of legends, is said to be unplayable on lower elos. His winrate statistics for mid is less than 50% if not 40%. Despite the odds I put in the work, grinded and lost a lot and it paid off. I'm on a 8 win-streak and just got a pentakill in the last game. Looking for more Azir plays in the future!
